title: Add a sessionless exec endpoint to the Libpod REST API

comments.body:
Hello @jeffrey-at-cohere ! how's going?

I am a prospective mentee for the upcoming LFX Mentorship program. I am familiar with the CNCF ecosystem and cloud-native environments. I would like to contribute to this issue.

could  be assigned to me ?

thank you in advance

This needs proper buy in from maintainer first before anyone spends time working on it as it is a large feature.

I am personally not convinced that adding dedicated endpoint and a custom wire protocol are worth it. I do agree the leaked conmon command is a bad design choice but I think there are easier ways to get rid of that than inventing a bunch of new stuff.
We already have a DB state for exit codes for the containers. We could just as well add another db entries for the removed exec session to allow a later inspect call to work without delaying the cleanup command from running. And then regularly prune the entries based on the time just like we have with the exit codes.
That needs no client side changes and we avoid the process leak then. We still would use conmon and db tracking then but I does not sounds like that is your bottleneck.

cc @mheon

@Luap99 

What is the use case for `podman exec --no-session` currently then? This already exists it just isn't exposed in the Libpod API, are there issues with using --no-session?

First, I will note that the current `podman exec --no-session` code is not really where I want it to be. Right now, it eliminates DB writes, but *not* the conmon process. Getting rid of Conmon would be a major step in further reducing resource utilization and speeding execution.

For the business of making this available via the REST API: The original intent was that this was mostly to be used within Podman (making healthchecks, which are just an exec call under the covers, leaner and more efficient) and HPC usecases (where we see hundreds of execs into the same container, and eliminating DB contention and minimizing locking is a very good thing for performance). Neither of these really required REST API support, so it wasn't part of the feature's scope.

I tend to agree with @Luap99 that, if the concern is more around Conmon sessions being left alive due to their exit delay, we should focus on fixing that instead. We already have a mechanism for preserving container exit codes for a time after the container is removed so `podman run` can still get them if a `podman rm --force` happens in another terminal. I don't see a good reason we couldn't do the same with exec sessions. That doesn't require a new API, cleans up the gross hack that is Conmon exit delay, and benefits everyone, not just users of the new API.
